components.name: Planificación Week (collapsible)
components.description: Reuses gym-tracker's own hist-session/hist-hdr/hist-body collapse pattern for plan weeks. Lunes and Viernes (when not set to Test) hold any number of named blocks, each its own 4-column field row (SERIES/DIST M/RITMO/REC) plus a name field and a remove (✕) control, with a dashed '+ Bloque' row to append another; Miércoles and a Viernes set to Test stay single-field. Edits land in a draft (planDraft), not DB.plan directly; a Cancelar/Guardar footer appears only when the draft differs from the saved week, and folding or switching weeks with a dirty draft asks for confirmation first.

narrative.overview:
This app (formerly '1000 m Tracker') is now KM Tracker, and this is the third correction of its visual direction: estudio keeps its own system, untouched; KM Tracker and gym-tracker are the pair that share one, copied component-by-component from gym-tracker's real index.html rather than approximated — the header, the today-hero, the day-grid (now LUN/MIÉ/VIE), the date pill, the vol-info-btn access row, the emom-card quick-register pattern, the profile-card/pstat trio, the etapa-badge zone chips, and the macros-style detail cards. Only two pieces of the earlier estudio-style build survive, re-skinned onto gym-tracker tokens by explicit request: the Sesiones row's flat dot-and-chevron list, and red for the Ajustes 'Eliminar' action.

The material is near-black frosted glass everywhere: translucent white-on-black cards over a slow-drifting three-color radial mesh (blue/lime/orange), with a near-invisible dot-grain texture on top. Big numbers are the loudest thing on screen in oversized Bebas Neue; everything administrative drops into small SF Mono. There is exactly one header in the whole app (not per-screen — it never changes), and it is position:fixed with a solid fill rather than gym-tracker's own position:sticky + backdrop-filter, because that literal combination visibly dragged on scroll — a known WebKit compositing bug, not a style choice. Cards never explain their own data in prose; a title and a number are the whole card.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black glass cards sharing one recipe: layered gradient fill, hairline border, glossy top-edge seam, shadow-card
Bebas Neue oversized numerals for hero/stat/PR/pstat values; SF Mono for every logged or computed data point
Exactly one fixed .header for the whole app (content never changes per screen) plus the floating pill bottom-nav with a spring-eased sliding indicator
Selected/active states invert to solid white-on-black, never a tinted accent
Static tri-color mesh background — no per-tab recoloring, no halo mechanic
No explanatory prose under a title/value — the data is the whole card

rules.name: The One-Header Rule
rules.body: Exactly one .header exists in the whole document, position:fixed (not gym-tracker's own position:sticky, which drags on scroll when combined with backdrop-filter), solid var(--bg) fill, a direct unwrapped child of body so no ancestor transform/filter/overflow can break the fixed positioning. Any title living inside scrolling content is never fixed or sticky — it scrolls normally.

rules.name: The Type-Owns-Its-Color Rule
rules.body: Each session type (series/rodaje/velocidad/test) keeps one fixed accent everywhere it appears — colors never migrate to generic chrome, and there is no per-tab background recoloring.

rules.name: The Data-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: Any value the user logged or the app computed from logged data renders in SF Mono; Bebas Neue is reserved for headline-scale numbers and short uppercase labels.

rules.name: The Equal-Grid Rule
rules.body: Every Planificación day block's field row is grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr) regardless of how many fields that day type needs — rodaje leaves 2 cells empty rather than using a narrower grid, so columns stay aligned across Lunes/Miércoles/Viernes.

rules.name: The No-Explainer Rule
rules.body: A card states its title and its data; it never adds a sentence teaching what the data means or why it matters. Short, conditional, data-driven warnings that fire only when a real threshold is crossed (e.g. cadencia below 165) are not explainers and stay.

rules.name: The Typed-Time Rule
rules.body: Every time-valued field shares one onTimeInput/onTimeBlur pair: typing digits-only live-formats right-to-left (last 2 digits = seconds, rest = minutes, under 3 digits displays bare), and a seconds component over 59 flags .time-error on blur and blocks that field's save action until fixed.

dos: Do keep exactly one fixed .header for the whole app; any other title scrolls with its content.
Do keep each session type's color fixed everywhere it appears — never per-tab background recoloring.
Do render every logged/derived value in SF Mono.
Do give every Planificación day block the same 4-column grid regardless of how many fields it uses.
Do treat the nav-indicator's colored glow, the today-hero's shine sweep, and the emom-action amber glow as intentional gym-tracker brand commitments, not defects to flatten.
Do let a title/value stand alone without an explanatory sentence under it, per the No-Explainer Rule.
Do route every time-valued input through the shared onTimeInput/onTimeBlur pair and block save on .time-error, per the Typed-Time Rule.
donts: Don't reintroduce Archivo/Archivo Narrow, a shifting background halo, or any other piece of the twice-retired estudio-style skin.
Don't move Planificación back into Ajustes; it is its own apartado (alongside Hechas) inside the Sesiones tab.
Don't give a day block with fewer fields a narrower or re-centered grid — empty placeholder cells keep columns aligned.

Don't convert the Sesiones row back to gym-tracker's own expandable-session pattern, or re-theme the Ajustes 'Eliminar' row's red away — those are the two deliberate exceptions; everything else, including Físico, is gym-tracker's own native pattern now.
Don't revert the header to position:sticky to match gym-tracker more literally — that combination is the bug this app's header was fixed to avoid.
